summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, COPD, insulin-dependent diabetes, and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for acute decompensated systolic heart failure and acute kidney injury, likely triggered by recent cocaine use and high-sodium food intake. He presented with worsening dyspnea, orthopnea, and ankle edema. Treatment included intravenous and oral diuretics to manage fluid overload, resulting in a 15-pound weight loss and improvement in symptoms. His kidney function improved with diuresis, and his insulin regimen was intensified due to poor glycemic control, with glargine increased to 50 units twice daily. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor daily weights, limit fluid and salt intake, avoid cocaine, and follow up with outpatient care.
problems: Acute on chronic decompensated systolic heart failure
Chronic airway obstruction, not elsewhere classified
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
